transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because I’ve barely been sleeping since this warehouse inspection I had to do for work. I just... I lie there in bed replaying bits of it in my head. And then, when I finally do manage to drift off, I wake up completely sweaty and wide awake, almost like I’m right back near that blast. It's just really starting to take a toll on me.
How long ago did that warehouse inspection take place?
It was about a week ago. That's when the inspection was, and when the explosion happened. So, yeah, all of this has been going on for just about a week now.

latest_inference.note: Given the symptoms (re-experiencing, arousal, sleep disturbance) occurring within one week of a traumatic event, the diagnosis is Acute Stress Disorder. PTSD (F43.1x) requires symptoms to persist for more than one month, and sleep disorders (F51.01, G47.00) are better explained by the trauma reaction.
